claim: Missed shared subject, verdict DISAGREE: the value type of the per-viewer view key `workingLayer`. Model §2.9 (l. 3392) gives its values as 'ground, a sky island's `PlatKey`, or an underground depth band'. V09 §2.4 types it `WorkingLayer = { layer: 'ground' } | { layer: 'sky'; key: PlatKey } | { layer: 'underground' }` and says 'the band is the view key `depthBand` alone (§2.9), never copied here'. §2.9 itself lists `depthBand` as the cut-away's band, and V04 §5.1 (2)'s Go there sets `workingLayer` to Below and `depthBand` to the band as two keys. The canon ruled the text (V09-XCONF-1: 'ground, a sky island's PlatKey, or the underground (its band the view key depthBand)'), but the base never took it. Since R4-02 the base itself reads the key: §8.4 draws the view's working layer whatever its `LayerSpec.visible`, and §8.8's tile key holds 'the model layers the view draws (their toggles and the working layer)'. A builder of §8.4 and §8.8 who follows §2.9 parses a depth band out of a key that V09 writes as `{ layer: 'underground' }`, and the band ends up stored in two keys.
required_change: Model §2.9's View state entry '`workingLayer` (per viewer: the layer the tools act on — ground, a sky island's `PlatKey`, or an underground depth band; V09 §4.2)' reads '`workingLayer` (per viewer: the layer the tools act on and the view draws whatever its visibility, §8.4 — ground, a sky island's `PlatKey`, or the underground, its band the view key `depthBand` alone, never copied into `workingLayer`; its value V09 §2.4's `WorkingLayer`, its switch V09 §4.2)'.

claim: ONE FIX with VV34-r4-01 (vol-V03-V04), this lane's model–V04 seam. V04's repair left it as a hand-off ('the base's text decides'). §2.7's support step (6) (b) lists 'a frame growth's extension of its deck, §3.2 (9)' among the ops that change a standing raised way, and `RaisedFoot`, §3.2 (9) and §4.11 have 'the raised way's re-derivation' extend the deck to the new ring. The support step that re-derivation runs spaces the stations evenly over the whole deck ((2)), and for a changed course (5) keeps only the key of a station within p ÷ 2. So a growth may move every old pier by up to p ÷ 2. V04 §3.5.0 *At an epoch* depends on the opposite. It says 'An epoch op removes no obstacle … so the element set it collapses is the one a regeneration of the same state collapses (T-V4-65)', with `Foundations.apply` collapse-only over `EpochScope.raised`, which V04 §3.10 and V06 W64 now say holds 'the frame growth's deck extension'. Re-spaced piers leave collapsed elements and pillars under no pier, unequal to a regeneration, so T-V4-65 cannot pass. A moved pier can also land in a plot S8 holed round its old ring, against (6) (b)'s reservation. Two builders, two behaviours.
required_change: VV34-r4-01's text: §2.7's support step (6) (b), after '… a frame growth's extension of its deck, §3.2 (9)), and none drops it.', adds 'A frame growth's extension keeps every station of the old deck — its key, position and support `ring` — and every span between them with its `use` and `reason`; (1)–(5) and the span rule run on the extension alone, from the old deck's last interior station to the deck's new end on the new ring, its stations' keys minted after the largest the way has held ((5)); so no pier of the old deck moves and no footing leaves (V04 §3.5.0 *At an epoch*).' The `RaisedFoot` comment's 'then extends the deck to the new ring' adds '(the old deck's stations kept, the support step's (6) (b))'. Scope's END: T110-2's frame-growth clause adds 'every station of the old deck at its key, position and ring after the growth'. V04's END: T-V4-65's at-epoch clause adds the aqueduct whose deck a frame growth extends over a chamber within its piers' reach, the collapsed set equal to a regeneration's.

claim: CATALOGUE-GAP (C-wall-raised x C-raised-history). §2.7's support step (6) (b) (iii) (base l.2601-2605) makes an enceinte's trace cross a standing raised way 'through one station on the deck at its level — the one nearest where the trace would cross, the trace bent along the deck to pass through it, the station never moved'. A locked or pinned one is crossed the same way at generation (l.2592-2593). §7.1's `bend.wall.raisedCrossing` row (l.10593), V06 §3.7.6 (5)'s second bullet (V06 l.1596-1598) and V09's line say the same, with no else. Two reachable cases have no such station. (1) None at deck level: (2) gives n = max(1, round(L ÷ p)) spans and n − 1 interior stations (l.2533-2534), so a raised way shorter than 1.5 p has none (under 12-22 m masonry, 6-12 m timber; V11 §3.24.2). Examples: a drawn short raised way, a short elevated link or viaduct. Nor does one whose every interior station is on a ramp or a stair, which (6) never takes. (2) The nearest is already another enceinte's crossing station: an epoch contraction or re-anchored stretch, or a second hand `drawWall`, within p ÷ 2 of a standing crossing. (3)'s 'each taking the nearest interior station not yet taken' (l.2548-2550) holds only at generation, so two bands would share one support whose `supports` entry 'reads its stretch's `condition`' — of two stretches. (b) forbids adding a station. The ramps, stairs and feet are a reservation, only a way or a channel may pass under a span, and V06 says 'a trace never waits for a raised way' (V06 l.1603). So builders would add a station, pass the wall under a span, refuse, or share the station. No bar runs either case: T110-2 (4) and T-V6-47 cross multi-span raised ways at one crossing.
required_change: §2.7's support step (6) (b) (iii), after 'the one nearest where the trace would cross', add: 'and not already another trace's crossing station; where the raised way holds no such station — a single span (n = 1), every interior station on a ramp or a stair, or every one taken — the trace takes none: it is bent past the nearer foot (`RaisedWayRecord.feet`; the other where that foot lies on the arena's outer ring), clear of its ramp or stair and the under-deck strip, and crosses the part-0 way that leaves that foot, where one does, at a ground gate by §4.2 S3 (4)'s gate law. The raised way stands wholly on one side of the trace, nothing of it changed, reported (V06's wall report at an epoch; the dry run's line for a hand edit)'. At generation (a)'s 'else one added' stands. Ends: (1) determinism: §7.1's `bend.wall.raisedCrossing` outcome cell adds '; where it holds no untaken station on the deck at its level, the trace bent past its nearer foot, a ground gate on the way beyond it (§2.7's support step (6) (b) (iii))'. (2) V06: §3.7.6 (5)'s second bullet adds the same clause. (3) V09: `bend.wall.raisedCrossing` gains words for the bend past the foot, ending with `button.showWhy`. (4) scope: §13.2 T110-2 (4) adds 'a hand `drawWall` across a declared one-span masonry viaduct, and an epoch contraction whose new ring meets an aqueduct within p ÷ 2 of the old ring's crossing station: the first bent past the nearer foot with a ground gate on the way beyond it, the second through the next untaken station; in both, every station, key, span and state of the raised way unchanged but that station's support'.

claim: CATALOGUE-GAP (C-vault-village): a village palisade across a `vault` span has two outcomes in two texts. §2.7's support step (6) (b) makes 'the under-deck strip of each `vault` span … a reservation on ground part 0 for every later way, trace, strip …', with the palisade listed among the ways of crossing 'the rest of its under-deck strip' (base l.2597-2600). Yet (iv) says the palisade 'abuts each support standing in its band and passes beneath every span' (l.2608-2609). V07 §3.5a (4) agrees with (iv): 'The trace passes beneath a span as an ordinary stretch' (V07 l.1600-1601). §4.13's `wall` row names only supports (l.8981). A `vault` span stands at the village rungs: `span.vaultCap` is 10 at THORP, HAMLET and VILLAGE (V11 l.3975), and V07 §3.5a (7) registers V04's arch-vault source at every village rung. A span crossing the perimeter's band is not 'wholly on hinterland faces', so `country` does not keep it open. Each `vault` span 'holds one arch vault at grade' (l.2635-2636): a chamber with walled-up arch mouths. So VS3's palisade, laid at a village derivation around a declared raised way (V07 §3.5a (1)), has two outcomes on one case: it runs through the arch vault's chamber (base (iv), V07 (4)), or it stops at a reserved strip and leaves the line open (base (b)'s reservation). T-V7-48 ('the palisade abuts each standing support in its band') runs no `vault` span. Two units state two outcomes for one case: MAJOR by R3-03 (b).
required_change: §2.7's support step (6) (b) (iv) reads: '(iv) a village palisade (`VillagePlan.palisade`) abuts each support standing in its band and each arch vault of a `vault` span there — the trace ending at the vault's two walled-up arch mouths, the chamber kept whole and closing the line between them — and passes beneath every `open` span, with no crossing station and no gate (V07 §3.5a (4))'. Ends: (1) V07: §3.5a (4)'s 'The trace passes beneath a span as an ordinary stretch' reads 'The trace passes beneath an `open` span as an ordinary stretch and abuts a `vault` span's arch vault at its two arch mouths, never laid through the chamber (§2.7's support step (6) (b) (iv))'. (2) pipeline: §4.13's raised-way `wall` row reads 'a village palisade abuts its supports and its `vault` spans' arch vaults, the deck passing over with no gate'. (3) V07: T-V7-48 adds 'a declared viaduct with a `vault` span standing in the planned palisade's band: the palisade ending at the vault's arch mouths, the chamber whole, 0 palisade stretches inside an arch vault's footprint and no gap in the line'.

claim: CATALOGUE-GAP (C-river-raised x C-harbour-raised). R4-09's last support run (§2.7's support step (6) (a), base l.2589-2591): where a station 'this run can neither slide nor omit within `maxClearSpanM` and `maxPierM`', it 'keeps the place the earlier run gave it, and the S7 part it meets gives way in that batch — a strip, plaza or square cut round its ring, a quay, pier, mole or castle path ending at the ring and resuming beyond it'. A strip, plaza or square is a face, so 'cut round' defines it. A quay, pier or mole is a way: '`quay` ways along the waterfront … piers as `pier` ways … moles, breakwaters, quays and piers are `pier` / `quay` ways in S7's L1 batch' (§4.8 l.7717-7723). A castle path is a `path` way (l.2281). 'Ending at the ring and resuming beyond it' does not say whether the way stays one connected way, routed round the ring inside its platform, or is split into two antenna ends either side of a pier, which may cut a quay plot's, a pier head's or a water gate's only path (§5.3's network invariant). The case is common. A generated viaduct or aqueduct crossing a `quay`-banked river or canal in town sets its bank stations as near the water as (3) allows: the river's clear span is held at or under `maxClearSpanM` (masonry 30 m, timber 20 m), and a generated course past it drops. S7 then lays the `quay` ways along those banks. The last run finds each bank station in a quay's corridor, unable to slide landward (the river span would pass `maxClearSpanM`), into the water, or be omitted. §4.8's lead ('gives way round its ring', l.7592-7593) and §4.1's S7 row ('cut round its ring or ended at it', l.4932) add no rule for the way. T110-2 (3) counts '0 piers in a … quay, pier or mole' but no connectivity. Peers' VM-R4T-01 and VPC-R4-01 rule S5b and S5c ways and the intervallum lane and keep this wording.
required_change: §2.7's support step (6) (a): 'a quay, pier, mole or castle path ending at the ring and resuming beyond it' reads 'a quay's, pier's or mole's platform cut round its ring as a strip is, and its way — or a castle path — bent round the ring inside its own face, its corridor beside the ring no narrower than its class's least width, so the way stays one connected way; where that face cannot hold the bend, the way ends at the ring on the water side and re-joins its shore's nearest way on the land side by the shortest lawful link in that batch, so every plot, pier head and gate keeps a path (§5.3's network invariant)'. Ends: (1) pipeline: §4.8's lead and §4.1's S7 row read 'the S7 part it meets cut or bent round its ring (§2.7's support step (6) (a))'. (2) scope: §13.2 T110-2 (3) adds 'a CITY masonry viaduct across a `quay`-banked river at its clear-span bound: both bank stations kept, each quay cut round its ring, each quay's way one connected way round the ring, and every quay plot and water gate reached (§5.3)'.

claim: §2.7's support step (6) (a) (R4-09's text, l. 2586-2591) runs the support step once more after S7's batches 'with every obstacle then standing (S5b's and S5c's ways; S7's strips, gate plazas, castle paths, quays, piers and moles)', and 'a station this run can neither slide nor omit within `maxClearSpanM` and `maxPierM` keeps the place the earlier run gave it, and the S7 part it meets gives way in that batch — a strip, plaza or square cut round its ring, a quay, pier, mole or castle path ending at the ring and resuming beyond it'. The failure rung names S7's parts only. Where what such a station meets is a part-0 way — an S5b main road or an S5c street laid across an S4 or S5b viaduct at generation, which §4.3 *Lattice and costs* (l. 5629-5632) lets cross the strip wherever the soffit clears ('and the support step's last run (*The slot*, below) slides the supports off it ((6) (a))'), or S7's intervallum lane — nothing gives way: the station keeps its place in the way's corridor, a pier standing in a street (VEW-r3-01's impossible result, which R4-09 removes after generation), and §4.3 states the slide as always succeeding. Reachable: masonry `pierSpacingM` 8-15 m against `maxClearSpanM` 30 m (V11 §3.24.2), so a METROPOLIS `through` or `primary` way crossing a viaduct obliquely occupies 30 m or more of deck and the two stations in it can neither slide within `slideMaxFactor` nor be omitted; at generation no squareness bound applies. T110-2 (3)'s list (setback, glacis, berm, moat, gate plaza, quay, pier, mole) bars no way corridor.
required_change: §2.7's support step (6) (a), after '… a quay, pier, mole or castle path ending at the ring and resuming beyond it — reported (`W_RAISED_CROSSING`).': 'Where such a station meets a part-0 way's corridor — an S5b or S5c way, or S7's intervallum lane — that way's crossing of the under-deck strip moves in that batch along the strip to the nearest place whose corridor clears every station, by §4.3's crossing shift (its vertices moved on ground part 0, the faces beside it following), reported (`W_RAISED_CROSSING`), so no pier stands in a way's corridor.' §4.3 *Lattice and costs* (pipeline's end): '… slides the supports off it ((6) (a))' → '… slides the supports off it, or, where a support can neither slide nor be omitted within its bounds, moves the way's crossing clear of it ((6) (a))'. §13.2's T110-2 (3) (scope's end): its list adds 'a way's corridor', with a METROPOLIS fixture whose S4 masonry viaduct a `through` way crosses obliquely over two stations: the way's crossing moved clear, reported, 0 piers in a way's corridor. (The adjudicator may rule another last rung — e.g. S5b's and S5c's ways keeping off the support rings at generation as after it, so the earlier run's place is always lawful — provided no pier stands in a way's corridor, no span or pier passes its bound and no course is dropped.)

claim: §2.7's support step (6) (b) (l. 2596-2598, R4-09's text): 'only an op that names the raised way changes it (its edits, V06 §3.19's ops, a landfall, a frame growth's extension of its deck, §3.2 (9)), and none drops it'. Read as written, 'none' covers 'its edits', yet a hand delete of a raised way drops it (§7.1 *Delete*; §7.4's row, l. 11365: 'a removed generated one stays removed'; §2.7 *Source and lifecycle*: 'a removal of a generated way is a suppression'). The meaning R4-09 states is that nothing laid later drops it; the rows that build the delete are explicit, so nothing built changes.
required_change: §2.7's support step (6) (b): 'and none drops it' → 'and no later work drops it'.

claim: The support step's last run at generation (§2.7 (6) (a), l. 2586–2591) treats S5b's and S5c's ways as obstacles, and 'a station this run can neither slide nor omit within `maxClearSpanM` and `maxPierM` keeps the place the earlier run gave it, and the S7 part it meets gives way'. It gives no outcome for an S5b or S5c way the station meets. §4.3's new generation half (l. 5629–5632) lets a later stage's way cross an unlocked raised way's strip anywhere its soffit meets *The clearance*. That way keeps off only ramps, stairs and feet, not the earlier run's pier rings, and §4.3 says the last run 'slides the supports off it' with no exception. §4.8's lead (l. 7590–7593) and §4.1's S7 row (l. 4932) name only the S7 part. A pier may be impossible to slide (both neighbouring spans must stay ≤ 1.5 × the band's top, 12 m for timber) and impossible to omit (merged clear span ≤ 20 m timber, 30 m masonry; V11 §3.24.2), for example a wide corridor under a timber viaduct or two ways close together. There an S5c street or S5b road under an S4 or S5b viaduct either keeps the pier in its corridor or is bent, depending on the builder. T110-2 (3) (l. 18412–18413) counts no pier in a way corridor, and its clause (5) covers epochs only. repair-r4-pipeline's hand-off 1 names this gap.

The adjudicator may rule another last rung, provided no pier stands in a way's corridor, no span or pier passes its bound and the raised way stands. END at scope: T110-2 (3) l. 18412–18413 adds 'or an S5b or S5c way's corridor' to its 0-pier list, with a CITY fixture whose S4 timber viaduct is crossed by a `through` S5b road and an S5c street at stations no slide or omission clears.

claim: V04's round-4 trigger names 'the frame growth's deck extension' among the epoch changes to a raised way (V04 §3.5.0 *At an epoch*, l. 1340–1343; §3.10, l. 2286–2289; §1b.2; T-V4-63), and V04 §3.5.0 keeps 'An epoch op removes no obstacle … so the element set it collapses is the one a regeneration of the same state collapses (T-V4-65; V06's T-V6-67)', `Foundations.apply` being collapse-only. Whether the extension keeps the old deck's stations is stated nowhere. §3.2 (9) (base l. 3667) and `RaisedFoot` (l. 2313–2317) say only 'the raised way's re-derivation then extends the deck to the new ring … as §4.11 continues a through-road'. The support step that re-derivation runs spaces the n − 1 interior stations evenly at L ÷ n over the whole deck ((2), l. 2534) and, for a changed course, keeps only the KEY of a station within p ÷ 2 of a former one ((5), l. 2572), so as L grows every old pier may move by up to p ÷ 2. Support step (6) (b) (l. 2596–2598) holds a standing raised way ('nothing laid later … moves, adds or omits a station') but lists 'a frame growth's extension of its deck, §3.2 (9)' among the ops that change it without saying how. T110-2's frame-growth clause tests only the foot's ends. One builder re-spaces the whole deck: old footings leave, V04's collapse-only `Foundations.apply` keeps elements `collapsed` and pillars standing under no pier (unequal to a regeneration, so T-V4-65's at-epoch bar fails), and a re-sited pier can land on a building raised since generation (plots and footprints are no obstacle of (3); S8 holed them round the old rings), against (6) (b)'s held reservation. Another builder keeps the old stations and lays stations on the extension only. The V04 repair left this as a hand-off ('the base's text decides'); the base's text does not decide it. Graded MAJOR: two builders, two behaviours, off the common path; the re-spacing reading's pier-in-a-building outcome would be a blocker's impossible result there.

The `RaisedFoot` comment's 'then extends the deck to the new ring as §4.11 continues a through-road' adds '(the old deck's stations kept, the support step's (6) (b))'.
